correctness.summary: Auxiliary graph for the lower-bound feasibility flow is built with edgeId starting at 1, breaking the e^1 reverse-edge pairing in DinicMaxFlow/DinicDfs and yielding an incorrect feasibility flow.
correctness.triggeringInput: n=2, s=0, t=1, one edge 0->1 with lower=1, upper=2. Dinic on the aux graph then mis-pairs reverse edges (first forward edge id 1 -> 1^1=0 sentinel).
correctness.rootCause: MinCostFlowAddEdge writes forward edge at *edgeId then reverse at *edgeId+1; DinicDfs uses flow[e^1] for the reverse residual. This only works when forward ids are even. Starting edgeId at 1 puts the first forward edge on an odd id so e^1 references the head-sentinel/index 0 and the wrong reverse edge, corrupting the residual graph and the computed flow that the method then copies into flow[].
correctness.suggestedFix: Set edgeId = 2 at initialization (as in the verified DinicMaxFlow test and MaxFlowLowerBounds).

perf.summary: Dead sumPos/sumNeg accumulation loop over all n vertices is computed but never read.
perf.currentCost: An O(n) pass (lines 36-37) with a per-iteration branch and two long accumulations whose results (sumPos, sumNeg) are never used anywhere afterward.
perf.proposedChange: Delete lines 36-37 entirely: 'long sumPos = 0, sumNeg = 0;' and the following 'for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { ... }'. Nothing downstream consumes these values.
perf.rationale: Removes a full O(n) loop, n branches, and 2n long adds from the hot path with zero observable effect. Pure dead-code elimination — Burst/JIT may not always remove it because b[] is written through a pointer and could be considered to have aliasing/observable reads.
perf.risk: None. Verified by grep that sumPos and sumNeg have no other readers in this method or file. Observable behavior (flow[], *result, return) is unchanged.
